author: Staff Writer
title: EDITORIAL: Lobbying by former Congress members targeted - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Writer ,
6 hours ago
Persuading a sitting congressman on how to vote or what bill to sponsor is an art. Some might prefer to call it a bidding war.
But it’s often a matter of who is doing the persuading. And, who better to twist your arm than someone who shared your experiences in getting elected, sat next to or near you and knows how the system works?
When term limits — or voters — send an elected member of Congress out to pasture they are often welcomed with open arms by lobbying firms or deep-pocketed industry representatives eager for their insight and influence.
They can make more money lobbying than what they were legally paid to represent their constituents.
We believe money plays too large a role in deciding the direction of our nation. And, the fewer the lobbyists the better.
We’re pleased to see a bipartisan proposal by former Florida governor and now U.S. Sen. Rick Scott and Sen. Elizabeth Warren.
While the two have butted heads before, they somehow came up with the same goal when introducing the Banning Lobbying and Safeguarding Trust (BLAST) Act, to permanently ban former members of the House of Representatives and Senate from lobbying Congress after leaving office.
In introducing the bill, Scott said: “When politicians use their time in public office to cash in after they leave government, the American people lose. Trust in our institutions is at an all-time low, and the revolving door between Capitol Hill and K Street is a big part of that.
“We need to restore the American people’s trust in their government, and that’s why I’m proud to introduce this bipartisan bill to put government clearly back on the side of the people. Our founders never intended public service to become a training ground for a lifetime of lobbying. Senator Warren and I are working to end this practice once and for all.”
Sen. Warren had this to say: “It’s simple: Members of Congress should spend their time in Washington serving the American people, not preparing to cash in big time with a cushy lobbying career after they leave office. It’s long past time to close the revolving door that’s corrupted our government and destroyed public trust in elected officials. This bipartisan bill is a no-brainer that Congress should pass now.”
The BLAST Act would control lobbyist registration and conduct by former members of Congress.
First, it bars former Members and elected officers from working as registered lobbyists, as defined by the Lobbying Disclosure Act.
It would outlaw them even making lobbying contacts, regardless of their registration status.
A press release from Scott’s office said the act includes language that prohibits making communications or appearances before members of Congress, congressional staff, or legislative offices with the intent to influence official action on behalf of private parties.
Finally, the bill would also address “shadow lobbying” by expanding existing lobbying restrictions to cover former lawmakers who are compensated for lobbying activities, even if they do not formally register as lobbyists or make direct lobbying contacts themselves, according to the press release.
If a person ignores the restrictions, it could result in up to five years in prison as well as civil penalties up to $50,000 per violation.
We’ve had our criticism of Scott in the past, but we’ll tip our hat to him and Warren for their work on this idea.
